key_audit_matters: Revenue recognition: Revenue from the sale of products is recognised when control over goods is transferred to a customer. The actual point in time when revenue is recognised varies depending on the specific terms and conditions of the sales contracts entered with customers. The Company has many customers operating in various geographies and sales contracts with customers have distinct terms relating to the recognition of revenue, the right of return and price adjustments. Revenue is a key performance indicator for the Company. Accordingly, there could be pressure to meet the expectations of investors/ other stakeholders and/ or to meet revenue targets stipulated in performance incentive schemes for a reporting period. There is a risk of fraud related to revenue being overstated by recognition in the wrong period or before control has passed during the year and at period end. Company's assessment of accrual towards rebates, discounts, returns, service level penalties and allowances require estimates and judgement and change in these estimates can have a significant financial impact.

outlook.statement: The Company is looking forward to good profit margins in the near future.

The Company is in the mode of expansion of the business which generally requires spending lot of money upfront leading to minimal profits in the initial years. All this expenditure will result in to revenues over a period of next two to three years.

The Company is committed to build the business operations within budget and considering that the business operates on a going concern basis, it is believed that financial position of the Company will improve further in near future.
The Reserve Bank of India has projected a moderation in growth to around 6.6% for FY 2026-27 amid global uncertainties, while domestic fundamentals remain robust.

Having returned to profitability and rebuilt its capital base, the Company enters FY 2026-27 from a position of considerably greater financial strength. Management's priorities for the coming year are: Profitable growth: Scale up revenue from the rationalised, higher-margin portfolio and improve capacity utilisation, while maintaining pricing discipline. Working capital efficiency: Reduce inventory levels, sustain the improvement in collections and generate positive operating cash flows. Deleveraging: Use internal accruals and improved cash conversion to reduce working capital borrowings and finance costs. Customer and product pipeline: Deepen relationships with existing customers, add new customers in regulated and semi-regulated markets, and develop new intermediates and personal-care actives. Operational excellence: Continue process optimisation, yield improvement, solvent recovery and cost reduction to protect margins against input-cost volatility. Compliance and quality: Maintain robust quality management systems aligned with revised Schedule M and customer audit requirements. While the operating environment remains competitive, Management believes that the measures taken in FY 2025-26 have laid a sound foundation for sustainable and profitable growth.

risks: The Board of Directors has put in place a risk management framework to identify elements of risk in different areas of operations and to develop policy for actions associated to mitigate the risks.
trade-policy uncertainty
shifting tariff regimes
geopolitical tension in West Asia
volatility in energy and freight costs
Raw material / input cost risk: Fluctuations in prices and availability of KSMs, solvents and basic chemicals can affect margins and delivery schedules.
Working capital and liquidity risk: High inventory levels and the nature of the intermediates business require significant working capital.
Leverage and interest rate risk: Borrowings of ₹45.33 crore expose the Company to interest rate changes.
Revenue and customer concentration risk: Dependence on a limited number of customers and products may impact revenue stability.
Regulatory and quality risk: Non-compliance with GMP (revised Schedule M), environmental or customer quality standards may disrupt operations.
Foreign exchange risk: Export realisations and imported inputs are exposed to currency fluctuations.
Human resources risk: Attrition of skilled technical personnel may affect operations.
Pricing pressure and competition from large Indian and Chinese producers, particularly in commoditised intermediates.
Volatility in prices and availability of KSMs, solvents and basic chemicals, a significant portion of which is sourced from China.
Global trade-policy uncertainty, including potential tariffs in key export markets and currency volatility.
Rising regulatory and EHS requirements that demand continuous investment in quality systems, documentation and pollution control.
Customer concentration inherent in the intermediates business, where a limited number of customers can account for a significant share of revenue.

Liquidity risk
Market risk (Foreign currency risk, Interest rate risk, Price risk)
